title: Margins at Ds optima beyond conditional centering and d_psi=1
statement: Asymptotic margin behavior outside the audited scalar conditionally centered class. DS18 resolves existence and empirical inhabitation positively for the exact off-(L) law X,Z iid Uniform[-1,1], S=(X,3X^2-1+Z), K=3: the +/-1/3 X-interval rule is a regular beta=0 DS17 root, the unique strict population global profiled optimum with fixed positive margins, and every sequence of exact global finite regular Ds optima converges to it and is exactly one-point exchange-stable. This proves that the DS14 margin-certified branch genuinely survives off (L), but only through a law-specific global-selection theorem. The literal population labels can be finite exchange-unstable (serialized boundary witness), practical ascent selection and robustness over a nontrivial law neighborhood remain open, and measured mix3 scans still do not prove uniqueness or branch completeness. Branches d_psi > 1 and d_lambda >= 2 remain open under their audited cardinality and vector-steering restrictions.
warning: Partially resolved by DS18 on one exact bounded off-(L) law. The theorem uses finite global optima and does not make the fixed-point gate sufficient for generic laws, prove practical basin selection, or authorize sample centering. Numerical mix3 searches remain windowed measured evidence.
